litigation.note: No significant or material orders were passed by Regulators, Courts or Tribunals which will impact the going concern status or the Company's future operations. No applications were made and no proceedings are pending under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 during the year. The statutory and secretarial auditors' reports contain no qualification, reservation, adverse remark or disclaimer, and no auditor reported any fraud under Section 143(12).

risks.note: Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a Risk with negative financial implications: 'Risk of failure in any of the elements of talent management can impact Sirca Paints ability to grow and provide services to its customers.' Mitigation is stated as following industry-best human resource practices to attract, develop, deploy and retain talent.

Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as a Risk with negative implications — 'Adverse Health and Wellness condition directly impacts on the health and morale of the employees besides productivity impact.' The same issue is treated as an opportunity through technical and personality-development training, since evolving technology requires employees with the right skills.

Flagged as a Risk with negative implications: 'In view of Global Warming, environmental sustainability has become very crucial for all businesses.' The Company's stated approach is to prevent pollution, reduce waste, minimise resource consumption, comply with applicable environmental legal requirements and encourage environmental protection among employees and suppliers.

Structural concentration disclosed in the BRSR customer profile: the retail channel — over 4,000 dealers plus 20+ branches and depots — accounts for approximately 70% of total revenue, and the OEM segment of approximately 900+ furniture and fixture manufacturers contributes nearly 30%. Performance therefore depends on the health of the dealer network and of organised furniture manufacturers.

The BRSR business-activity split shows 23.42% of turnover comes from Import & Trading of Paints products versus 76.58% from Manufacturing of Paints, leaving roughly a quarter of turnover exposed to imported supply, landed-cost and currency conditions rather than in-house production.

The entity's disclosed business activities accounting for 90% of turnover are wholly within paints and coatings (manufacturing plus import and trading), with the Directors confirming there was no change in the nature of the Company's business during the year — leaving earnings exposed to a single end-industry cycle.
